To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the superconducting state of a metal is a macroscopic quantum phenomenon, (2) the electrons in a superconductor form a Bose‐Einstein condensate, and (3) this condensate is the ground state of the metal.

(1) the critical temperature of a superconductor can be raised by doping it with a magnetic impurity, (2) the critical temperature can be lowered by adding a nonmagnetic impurity, (3) the critical temperature depends on the magnetic field at the impurity site, (4) the impurities act as local magnetic moments, and (5) the critical temperature is lowered if a nonmagnetic atom replaces a magnetic atom.
